# i18n.py

[简体中文](i18n.zh.md) ｜ **English** ｜ [← Back to README](../README.en.md)

Runtime message localisation.

malight's errors, notices and export messages are **English by default**; one line switches
them to Chinese:

```python
import malight
malight.set_language("zh")      # switch to Chinese
malight.set_language("en")      # back to English, the default
```

If you would rather not touch the code, use the environment variable - handy for CI and
command-line scripts:

```bash
set MALIGHT_LANG=zh             # Windows
export MALIGHT_LANG=zh          # macOS / Linux
set MALIGHT_LANG=auto           # follow the system language
```

Precedence: `set_language()` > `MALIGHT_LANG` > the default `"en"`.

Only **runtime messages** are affected, never API names or returned data: machine-readable
values such as `kind` and `cmd` are always English ASCII so programs can rely on them.

Adding your own language (Traditional Chinese, Japanese, ...):

```python
from malight import i18n

i18n.add_messages("fr", {"export.ok": "[malight] {kind} export OK{tail} -> {path} [{size}]"})
malight.set_language("fr")      # untranslated keys fall back to English
```

Temporary switch, with no global side effect (useful in tests or doc generation):

```python
with malight.use_language("zh"):
    pen.export_png()            # these lines print Chinese
```

## Classes and methods

### Functions

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `normalize` | Normalise any way of writing a language down to its family: en, zh or auto. |
| `get_language` | The language code currently in effect, after message fallback, i.e. the one lookups use. |
| `set_language` | Set the output language globally, taking precedence over the environment variable. |
| `reset_language` | Drop the explicit setting and go back to the environment-variable or default-English result. |
| `is_chinese` | Whether messages are currently being output in Chinese. |
| `t` | Look up one localised message and format it with keyword arguments. |
| `available_languages` | The language codes that currently have messages registered. |
| `add_messages` | Register or extend the messages of a language; missing keys fall back to the language family, then to English. |

### `Language`

Language enum; it subclasses str so it can be used as a plain string.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `of(value)` | Normalise any spelling into a Language member. |

### `use_language`

Temporarily switch language; the previous setting is restored on exit.

## Full example

Run it directly in PyCharm, or from the command line: `python malight/i18n.py`

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import malight
    from malight import i18n

    # 1) The language enum subclasses str: compare it with plain strings
    print("enum    :", Language.EN, Language.ZH, "| ZH_CN is ZH:", Language.ZH_CN is Language.ZH)
    print("compare :", Language.ZH == "zh", Language.EN == "en")

    # 2) Normalisation accepts every spelling and falls back to English
    for raw in ("zh", "zh-CN", "zh_CN", "chs", "Chinese", "en-US", "japanese", None):
        print("  normalize({!r:>10}) -> {}".format(raw, i18n.normalize(raw)))

    # 3) English by default, with the environment variable overriding it
    print("default :", malight.get_language(), "(ENV {}={!r})".format(
        i18n.ENV_VAR, os.environ.get(i18n.ENV_VAR)))

    # 4) The same message in both languages: export info and an error
    key = "export.ok"
    kw = dict(kind="PNG", tail="", path=r"C:\out\demo.png", size="12.3 KB")
    for code in ("en", "zh"):
        malight.set_language(code)
        ok, err = malight.t(key, **kw), malight.t("err.need_shapely")
        print("[{}] export : {}".format(code, ok, code, ok))
        print("[{}] error : {}".format(code, err, code, err))

    # 5) is_chinese / available_languages
    malight.set_language("zh")
    print("is_chinese  :", malight.is_chinese())
    print("built-in languages :", malight.available_languages())

    # 6) use_language switches temporarily and restores on exit
    with malight.use_language("en"):
        print("inside :", malight.t("size.unknown"))
    print("after  :", malight.t("size.unknown"))

    # 7) Add your own language; untranslated keys fall back to English
    malight.add_messages("zh-TW", {
        "export.ok": "[malight] {kind} export OK{tail} -> {path}  [{size}]",
        "size.unknown": "size unknown",
    })
    malight.set_language("zh-TW")
    print("zh-TW       :", malight.t(key, **kw))
    print("untranslated fallback :", malight.t("err.no_board"), "  <- fell back to English")
    print("languages now :", malight.available_languages())

    # 8) Reset: back to the environment variable or default English
    print("after reset   :", malight.reset_language())
```
